campbell.title: Campbell City Council — October 6, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council's October 6, 2026, agenda listed routine business such as approving bills, treasurer's reports, and meeting minutes, alongside a proclamation for Breast Cancer Awareness Month. It also included items on a large state grant application for park development, consultant and compensation agreements, a City Manager salary adjustment, and appointments to two advisory bodies.
keyTopics: Proclamation recognizing October 2026 as Breast Cancer Awareness Month, honoring El Camino Health's breast cancer care efforts
Resolution authorizing an $8,500,000 grant application to the California Department of Parks and Recreation's Statewide Park Development and Community Revitalization Program
Agreement for Consultant Services with Atchison, Barisone and Condotti, LLP, including dispensing with standard bidding requirements
Resolutions amending compensation and working conditions for unrepresented Confidential, Classified Management, and Unclassified Management employees, plus a City Manager salary adjustment
Appointments to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee and the Civic Improvement Commission

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — October 7, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council's October 7, 2026, agenda listed routine items like meeting minutes, check registers, and a treasurer's report, alongside a $2.5 million budget amendment for the Hakone Gardens Koi Pond Renovation Project. Other notable items included a proposed no-parking zone on Chester Avenue, a discussion on whether to switch the city's long-term law enforcement provider to Los Gatos Monte Sereno Police Department, a comparison of animal care service providers, and a public hearing on annual updates to the city code.
keyTopics: Hakone Gardens Koi Pond Renovation Project budget amendment for $2,500,000
No Parking Anytime zone proposed for a section of Chester Avenue
Discussion on switching the city's law enforcement provider to Los Gatos Monte Sereno Police Department
Comparison of regional animal care service providers, including continuing with San Jose Animal Care and Services
Public hearing on annual city code updates covering appeals scheduling, commissioner qualifications, and business record retention

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 22, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council agenda for September 22, 2026, included a wastewater treatment agreement with Palo Alto and Mountain View, a VTA board appointment, and an urgency ordinance on detention and custodial facilities. The agenda also listed appointments to city commissions and an amendment to the city's legal services contract.
keyTopics: Addendum No. 14 to the Regional Water Quality Control Plant Basic Agreement with Palo Alto and Mountain View
Reappointment of Councilmember Jonathan Weinberg to the VTA Board for Group 2 (north counties)
Interim urgency ordinance establishing a temporary moratorium on applications for detention or custodial facilities and custodial-processing facilities
Appointments to the Complete Streets, Environmental, and Planning Commissions
Amendment No. 1 to the legal services agreement with Berliner Cohen, LLP, setting a $21,500 monthly retainer for up to 70 hours plus a $385 hourly rate

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — October 6, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council's October 6, 2026, agenda included routine business such as approving minutes and payroll reports, along with a few procedural and policy items. Notable items included a contracting issue involving Denali Tree Services, an amendment to an existing agreement, and a proposed update to the town's purchasing policy. The agenda also listed receipt of the July 2026 financial reports and an updated work plan from the Finance Commission.
keyTopics: Relieving Denali Tree Services of its bid due to a bidder's mistake
Authorizing the Town Manager to execute a first amendment to an existing agreement
Adopting a resolution amending the Town's Purchasing Policy (Policy 4-06)
Approving the Finance Commission's updated 2026 work plan
Receiving the July 2026 expenditure and revenue reports

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — October 7, 2026
san-jose.summary: This is a San José Rules and Open Government Committee agenda. The October 13, 2026, meeting was cancelled, and the committee was set to review the draft agenda for October 20, 2026. Other listed items include routine reports, a proclamation for Taiwan Retrocession Day, and a proposal on self-checkout safety standards at grocery and drug retail stores.
keyTopics: October 13, 2026, meeting cancelled
Review of the draft agenda for October 20, 2026
Proclamation, flag raising, and lighting recognizing Taiwan Retrocession Day (sponsored by Council District 5)
Proposal on self-checkout safety standards for grocery and drug retail stores (Candelas and Cohen)
Routine reports: City Clerk's public record, City Auditor's monthly activity report, and a joint special meeting with the Santa Clara Valley Water District

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Council Sustainability Committee — September 29, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The agenda for Mountain View's Council Sustainability Committee meeting includes a draft Five-Year Community Decarbonization Plan and the 2024 Community Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory. The meeting was set up with both in-person and virtual/phone participation options for residents.
keyTopics: Draft Five-Year Community Decarbonization Plan
2024 Community Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — October 6, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council agenda for October 6, 2026, includes recognitions such as the Little League Junior Division All-Stars, Indigenous Peoples' Day, Friends of the Library Week, and Sunnyvale Stands United Against Hate Week. The agenda also lists routine approvals, a contract amendment for environmental consulting at the SMaRT Station and landfill, a PG&E easement over Clean Water Facility land, and public hearings on nonfunctional turf irrigation restrictions, a service worker retention ordinance, and public art for the Lakewood Park renovation.
keyTopics: Ordinance to prohibit potable water use for nonfunctional turf irrigation under AB 1572
Introduction of a Service Worker Retention Ordinance
Public art approval for Lakewood Park renovation
Contract amendment with WSP USA for environmental consulting at SMaRT Station and Sunnyvale Landfill
PG&E easement over a portion of the Clean Water Facility

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — October 6, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council's agenda includes closed-session discussions on potential litigation and a real estate negotiation with the Cupertino Union School District over property on Finch Avenue, plus routine consent items like meeting minutes and treasurer's reports. The agenda also lists a public hearing on conduit financing for The Rise project and a public information session on an approved soil contamination remediation plan at that same site.
keyTopics: Closed session on anticipated litigation (one potential case)
Real property negotiation for 10480 Finch Avenue with Cupertino Union School District, including an exchange agreement listed at an $11.8 million negotiated purchase price
Resolution to increase employer contributions for retiree medical/hospitalization insurance under PEMHCA for pre-August 2004 hires
Grant application for $80,000 under the Rubberized Pavement Grant Program
Public information session on the approved soil contamination remediation plan at The Rise, plus a TEFRA public hearing on conduit financing for the project

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council and Authorities Concurrent — October 6, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara City Council and Stadium Authority Board have a joint agenda combining a dinner meeting with the Parks and Recreation Commission and a 7 PM regular meeting. The agenda includes proclamations, routine consent items, a report on pedestrian access restrictions on Lawrence and San Tomas Expressways, a staff presentation on data center development policy, and several councilmember requests related to data centers and neighborhood parking issues.
keyTopics: Report and potential Council action on pedestrian access restrictions on portions of Lawrence and San Tomas Expressways
Stadium Authority financial status report for the quarter ending June 30, 2026, with possible budget amendments
Staff presentation on updating city policies for new data center development, covering water usage and grid support participation
Councilmember Hardy's requests on data center power allocation processes (with a possible moratorium option) and a proposed ban on non-disclosure agreements with data centers

Councilmember Park's deferred requests on resident parking near apartment complexes, compensation for vehicles ticketed/towed during stadium events, and parking requirements for affordable housing projects

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council agenda for September 15, 2026, listed items on federal housing and community development funding, red light camera traffic safety, and the condition of the Milpitas Community Center. The agenda also included financial actions related to the former Redevelopment Agency's successor entity, including a bond refunding resolution.
keyTopics: Approval of the Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated Plan
Presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program
Presentation on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolution of the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency board
Resolution authorizing the sale and issuance of refunding bonds for the Successor Agency

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee — October 2, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee's agenda for October 2, 2026, included staff and committee member comments, plus an update on long duration resiliency for the electric system. A late-added staff report noted this item was determined not to be a project under CEQA.
keyTopics: Update on Electric System Long Duration Resiliency, with a staff presentation
CEQA status for the resiliency item determined as Not a Project
Staff comments
Committee member comments and announcements
